chunks: Al-Saffar from Ali ibn Isma'il from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from al-Husayn ibn Abdillah from his father from his grandfather from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said:
"If a man has multiple horses during the expedition (ghazw), shares (sahm) are allotted only for two of them."

key_terms.أَفْرَاسٌ: Plural of horse, referring to cavalry mounts
key_terms.يُسْهَمْ: Verb form meaning 'to be allotted a share' or 'to receive a portion'

ai.seo_question: How many horses' shares are counted for war booty distribution in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of moderation in military logistics, limiting the soldier's share of war booty to two horses to prevent excessive accumulation by the wealthy. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on equitable distribution (*fay'*) and practical military efficiency, ensuring that surplus resources do not create disparity among the fighters. The ruling underscores the Prophetic tradition of balancing individual capability with communal fairness in the context of *jihad*.
